subject: Hospitality
title: The First Restaurants
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The First Restaurants.

hook.text: The word 'restaurant' comes from French 'restaurer'—to restore. The first ones sold restorative broths, not full meals.

buildup.text: In 1765, a Parisian named Boulanger sold soups outside the guild system. He called his shop a 'restaurant' for the weary.

discovery.text: After the French Revolution, unemployed chefs from aristocratic households opened restaurants for the public instead.

twist.text: Restaurants were a democratic revolution—for the first time, anyone with money could eat food once reserved for the elite.

climax.text: By 1814, Paris had over 3,000 restaurants. The concept spread across Europe and then the world.

punchline.text: Born from revolution, fueled by unemployed chefs. Restaurants are democratic.

quiz.question: Why did French aristocratic chefs open restaurants after the Revolution?
options: Their employers lost power and they needed new customers
